topics.title: Asking the right question and recording answers

learn.hook: 'Do you like school?' or 'Which subject do you like most: Maths, English, EVS or Hindi?' Which question gives better data?
points: A good survey question is clear and gives the information you need.
Giving choices helps: 'Which is your favourite subject: Maths, English, EVS or Hindi?'
Record answers quickly with short codes: M for Maths, E for English, V for EVS, H for Hindi.
Data can be shown as a long list of codes or as a table of counts. A table is much easier to read.
Choose the way of showing data that answers questions fastest.

example.q: Codes recorded: M E M V H M E M V M. How many chose Maths?

learn.reallife: Teachers, shopkeepers and the government run surveys to plan things like school timetables, stock and new roads.

games.title: Good survey question?
items: Which fruit do you like most: mango, banana or apple?
How do you come to school: walk, bus, cycle or car?
How many brothers and sisters do you have?

games.title: Count the codes (M E V H)

items.q: M M E V M: how many M?
E E H V E: how many E?
V H V V M V: how many V?
H M H E: how many H?
M E M V H M E M: total answers

quiz.q: Which is the best survey question to find classmates' favourite sport?
options: Which sport do you like most: cricket, football, kabaddi or badminton?
quiz.explain: It is clear and gives choices, so the answers can be counted.

quiz.q: Riya records favourite subjects as M, E, V, H. What does V stand for?
quiz.explain: V is the short code for EVS.

quiz.q: Codes: M E M V H M E. How many children chose English (E)?
Codes: M E M V H M E. How many children answered in all?
quiz.explain: There are 7 codes, one per child.

quiz.q: Which way of showing data is easier to read: a long list of codes, or a table of counts?
quiz.explain: A table shows each total at once, so we do not need to count again.
quiz.mistake: Does not compare ways of showing data

quiz.q: Why do we use short codes when recording answers?
quiz.explain: Codes save time when many people answer.
quiz.mistake: Does not see the use of codes

quiz.q: Codes: M M E V M H M. Which subject is the favourite?
Raju asks 'Do you like food?' Everyone says yes. What is wrong with his question?
options: It does not tell which food they like
quiz.explain: A yes/no question cannot show favourites. He should list food choices.
quiz.mistake: Thinks any question gives useful data

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know the class's favourite fruit. Help Gappu ask a good question and record the answers.
teach.praise: I asked 'Mango, banana or apple?', wrote codes and made a table. Mango wins!
teach.nudge: What makes a good question, and how will you record and show the answers?

learn.hook: Which fruit does your class love most? Don't guess. Ask everyone and count. That's data!
points: Data is information we collect, like answers to a question or things we count.
We can collect data by asking people (a survey) or by watching and counting.
Tally marks help us count fast: 4 lines and a 5th line across make a bundle of 5.
We put the counts in a table so it is easy to read and compare.
From a table we can find the most, the least, the total and the difference.

example.q: In a survey, 12 children chose mango, 8 chose banana and 5 chose apple. How many children took part, and which fruit is the favourite?
steps: The biggest count is 12, for mango.

learn.reallife: Teachers collect data on attendance. Cricket scorers keep data on runs and wickets.

games.title: Data facts
items: A survey means asking people questions and noting their answers.
That is one way to collect data.
In tally marks, the 5th line goes across the other 4.
Guessing is a good way to collect data.
We must ask or count to get real data.
A table makes data easier to read.
Counts are neatly lined up to compare.
If mango has 12 votes and apple has 5, apple is more popular.
12 is more than 5, so mango is more popular.

quiz.q: Arjun's tally for red cars has 2 bundles of five and 3 more lines. How many red cars did he count?
quiz.explain: 2 bundles of five = 10. 3 more lines make 13.

quiz.q: In a survey, 12 children chose mango, 8 chose banana and 5 chose apple. How many children took part?
quiz.mistake: Adds only two of the fruits

quiz.q: In the same survey (mango 12, banana 8, apple 5), which fruit is the favourite?
quiz.mistake: Picks the fruit with the smallest count

quiz.q: How many more children chose mango (12) than apple (5)?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Riya wants to know how her classmates come to school. What is the best way to collect this data?
options: Ask each child and make tally marks
Guess from looking at the gate once
Count the bicycles at her home
quiz.explain: Asking every child and keeping a tally gives correct, complete data.
quiz.mistake: Thinks asking one person or guessing is enough

quiz.q: A table of favourite colours shows Red 9, Blue 6, Green 9, Yellow 4. Which two colours got the same number of votes?
quiz.explain: Red and Green both have 9 votes.

quiz.q: Kabir counted vehicles passing his school: 14 cars, 23 bikes and 9 buses. How many vehicles did he count?
In Kabir's count (14 cars, 23 bikes, 9 buses), how many fewer buses than bikes were there?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two numbers instead of subtracting

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know the favourite sweet of all the birds in the forest. How should Gappu find out?
teach.praise: Yes! Ask everyone, count with tally marks and write it in a table. Gappu will find the favourite sweet!
teach.nudge: Should Gappu just guess? What should Gappu do with each answer?

learn.hook: Tall bars, short bars! A bar graph lets you compare data in one quick look.
points: A bar graph uses bars to show data. A taller (or longer) bar means a bigger number.
Read the number at the end of each bar using the scale on the side.
The scale can go up in 1s, 2s, 5s or 10s. Check it before reading!
We can use a bar graph to find the most, the least, the total and the difference.

example.q: A bar graph shows rangoli kits sold: Monday 4, Tuesday 7, Wednesday 3, Thursday 6. Which day sold the most, and how many were sold in all?

learn.reallife: TV news shows bar graphs of rainfall, cricket runs per over and votes.

games.title: Bars from shortest to tallest
games.prompt: Rainy days: June 8, July 15, August 12, September 6. Order from fewest to most.

games.title: Bar graph facts
items: A taller bar shows a bigger number.
The height of a bar shows the amount.
The scale on a bar graph must always go up in 1s.
It can go up in 2s, 5s, 10s and so on.
Two bars of the same height show the same number.
The shortest bar shows the most popular choice.
The tallest bar shows the most popular choice.
If each line stands for 2, a bar reaching the 6th line shows 12.

quiz.q: A bar graph shows rangoli kits sold: Mon 4, Tue 7, Wed 3, Thu 6. On which day were the most kits sold?
quiz.explain: Tuesday has the tallest bar, 7 kits.
quiz.mistake: Picks the day with the shortest bar

quiz.q: Rangoli kits sold were Mon 4, Tue 7, Wed 3, Thu 6. How many more kits were sold on Tuesday than on Wednesday?
quiz.mistake: Adds the two bars instead of finding the difference

quiz.q: Rangoli kits sold were Mon 4, Tue 7, Wed 3, Thu 6. How many kits were sold in the 4 days altogether?
A bar graph of favourite games shows Cricket 15, Kabaddi 10, Kho-kho 5, Football 10. Which two games have bars of the same height?
quiz.explain: Kabaddi and Football both have 10 votes, so their bars are the same height.
quiz.mistake: Does not read the bar values carefully

quiz.q: On a bar graph, each line on the scale stands for 2 students. A bar reaches the 6th line. How many students does it show?
quiz.mistake: Reads the line number without using the scale

quiz.q: In the favourite games graph (Cricket 15, Kabaddi 10, Kho-kho 5, Football 10), which game is liked the least?
quiz.explain: Kho-kho has the shortest bar, only 5 votes.
quiz.mistake: Picks the tallest bar instead of the shortest

quiz.q: What does a taller bar in a bar graph show?
quiz.explain: The taller the bar, the bigger the number it shows.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bar height has no meaning

quiz.q: A bar graph shows rainy days: June 8, July 15, August 12, September 6. How many rainy days were there in July and August together?
quiz.mistake: Finds the difference instead of the total

teach.ask: Gappu sees a bar graph of fruits but doesn't know how to read it. What should Gappu look at?
teach.praise: Thank you! Taller bars mean more, and the scale tells the exact number. Gappu can read graphs now!
teach.nudge: What does a taller bar mean? Where does Gappu read the number?

topics.title: Colourful golas: reading and making pictographs

learn.hook: The gola-wala sold rose, mango, khus and orange golas. Which flavour should he buy more syrup for?
points: To make a picture chart, colour or draw one symbol for each group of data, using the key.
Read a pictograph: count symbols and multiply by the key value.
The row with the most symbols shows the most popular item; the fewest shows the least.
Use data to decide: buy more of the most popular flavour.
Data can be split into groups, like boys and girls, to compare them separately.

example.q: Using the gola pictograph (key 🍧 = 2), how many mango golas were sold?

learn.reallife: Shopkeepers look at what sells most before ordering new stock. That is using data to decide!

quiz.q: Gola pictograph (key 🍧 = 2 golas). Rose: 🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Mango: 🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Khus: 🍧🍧 | Orange: 🍧🍧🍧. Which flavour was sold the most?
Gola pictograph (key 🍧 = 2 golas). Rose: 🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Mango: 🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Khus: 🍧🍧 | Orange: 🍧🍧🍧. How many rose golas were sold?
quiz.mistake: Counts symbols without using the key

quiz.q: Gola pictograph (key 🍧 = 2 golas). Rose: 🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Mango: 🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Khus: 🍧🍧 | Orange: 🍧🍧🍧. Which flavour was sold the least?
Gola pictograph (key 🍧 = 2 golas). Rose: 🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Mango: 🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Khus: 🍧🍧 | Orange: 🍧🍧🍧. The gola-wala can buy only one big bottle of syrup. Which flavour should he choose?
quiz.explain: Mango sells the most, so it is the best choice.
quiz.mistake: Does not use the data to decide

quiz.q: Gola pictograph (key 🍧 = 2 golas). Rose: 🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Mango: 🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧🍧 | Khus: 🍧🍧 | Orange: 🍧🍧🍧. How many more mango golas than khus golas were sold?
Boys bought 5 rose golas and girls bought 9. Using 🍧 = 1, how many symbols for girls?
quiz.explain: Each symbol is 1 gola, so 9 symbols.

quiz.q: Boys: rose 5, mango 7. Girls: rose 9, mango 4. Which flavour do girls like more?
Boys: rose 5, mango 7. Girls: rose 9, mango 4. Which flavour sold more in total?

teach.ask: Gappu's gola chart has 🍧 = 2. The mango row has 6 symbols. Gappu says 6 mango golas were sold. Help!
teach.praise: Each symbol is 2 golas, so 6 × 2 = 12 mango golas!
teach.nudge: What does the key tell you about each symbol?

learn.hook: Can a picture of one star stand for 5 children? In a pictograph it can!
points: A pictograph shows data using pictures or symbols.
The key tells how much one symbol stands for, like ⭐ = 5 children.
To read a row, multiply the number of symbols by the key value.
Half a symbol stands for half the key value. If ⭐ = 4, half a star = 2.
To draw a row, divide the number by the key value to find how many symbols.

example.q: Key: each ⭐ = 5 children. The cricket row has 4 stars. How many children like cricket?

learn.reallife: Newspapers and school notice boards use pictographs to show data in a fun way.

items.q: Key 🌟 = 4. Row has 2 and a half 🌟

items.text: Key 🪁 = 5 kites. To show 25 kites, draw ___ symbols.
Key 🚌 = 10 children. To show 40 children, draw ___ symbols.
Key 🍪 = 4 cookies. To show 12 cookies, draw ___ symbols.
Key ⭐ = 2 votes. Half a star stands for ___ vote.

quiz.q: Key: each ⭐ = 5 children. The cricket row has 4 stars. How many children like cricket?
quiz.mistake: Counts the stars but forgets the key

quiz.q: Key: each ⚽ = 10 children. The football row has 3 balls. How many children like football?
quiz.mistake: Adds the key value instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Key: each 🪁 = 5 kites. A shop sold 25 kites. How many kite symbols should the row have?
quiz.mistake: Draws one symbol for every kite

quiz.q: Key: each 🍪 = 4 cookies. A row shows 3 full cookies and half a cookie. How many cookies is that?
quiz.mistake: Ignores the half symbol, or counts it as a full one

quiz.q: Key: each 📚 = 10 books. Monday has 2 symbols and Tuesday has 5 symbols. How many more books were borrowed on Tuesday?
quiz.explain: Tuesday has 5 - 2 = 3 more symbols. 3 × 10 = 30 more books.
quiz.mistake: Gives the difference in symbols (3) instead of books

quiz.q: Why does a pictograph need a key?
options: To tell how much one symbol stands for
quiz.explain: The key tells us the value of one symbol, so we can read the numbers.

quiz.q: Key: each 🚌 = 10 children. How should 40 children be shown?
quiz.mistake: Draws one symbol for each child

quiz.q: Key: each 😊 = 3 children. Class A has 4 symbols and Class B has 6 symbols. How many children are there in both classes?
quiz.mistake: Counts symbols without using the key

teach.ask: Gappu sees a pictograph with 5 apple pictures but the key says 🍎 = 2 apples. Gappu says 5 apples. Is that right?
teach.praise: Thanks! Each picture is 2 apples, so 5 × 2 = 10 apples. Always read the key!
teach.nudge: What does the key tell Gappu about each apple picture?

topics.title: Chess or cricket? A survey with two choices

learn.hook: Some children play only chess, some only cricket, some both and some neither. How do we sort them?
points: Ask each child two questions: Do you play chess? Do you play cricket?
Sort answers into 4 groups: only chess, only cricket, both, neither.
Record the counts in a table.
Children who play chess = only chess + both. Children who play cricket = only cricket + both.

example.q: Only chess 6, only cricket 10, both 4, neither 3. How many play cricket?

learn.reallife: Schools use surveys like this to plan clubs and sports periods.

games.title: Which group?
items: Chess club member who never plays cricket
Cricket team captain who also plays chess
Bowler who does not play chess

games.title: Survey table: only chess 6, only cricket 10, both 4, neither 3

quiz.q: Survey: only chess 6, only cricket 10, both 4, neither 3. How many play chess?
Same survey. How many play cricket?
Same survey. How many children were asked in all?
Same survey. Do more children play chess or cricket?
Same survey. How many play both games?
quiz.explain: The table shows 4 in the 'both' group.

quiz.q: Sunil plays cricket and chess. In which group should he be recorded?
A child plays neither game. Which group?
quiz.explain: Neither means plays none of the two.

quiz.q: Same survey. How many play only one of the two games?

teach.ask: Gappu surveyed friends about chess and cricket. Some play both! How should Gappu record and count?
teach.praise: Four groups: only chess, only cricket, both, neither. For cricket players, I add only cricket and both!
teach.nudge: Which groups do you need, and how do you count all the cricket players?

topics.title: Bal Mela: reading sales over days

learn.hook: At the school Bal Mela, popcorn and balloons sold out fast. Which day was the busiest?
points: A pictograph can show sales on different days. Read each day's row using the key.
Total for an item = add all its days. Total for a day = add all items on that day.
The day with the most sales has the biggest total.
Always check the key first: 🍿 = 10 packets means 3 symbols = 30 packets.

example.q: Using the popcorn pictograph (🍿 = 10), how many packets were sold over the three days?

learn.reallife: Organisers of fairs and melas count sales each day to plan stock and stalls for the next year.

games.title: Popcorn chart (🍿 = 10): Mon 3, Tue 5, Wed 4 symbols
Balloon chart (🎈 = 5): Mon 4, Tue 3, Wed 6 symbols
items: Tuesday sold more balloons than Monday.

quiz.q: Bal Mela popcorn sales (key 🍿 = 10 packets). Mon: 🍿🍿🍿 | Tue: 🍿🍿🍿🍿🍿 | Wed: 🍿🍿🍿🍿. How many packets were sold on Tuesday?
Bal Mela popcorn sales (key 🍿 = 10 packets). Mon: 🍿🍿🍿 | Tue: 🍿🍿🍿🍿🍿 | Wed: 🍿🍿🍿🍿. On which day were the most packets sold?
Bal Mela popcorn sales (key 🍿 = 10 packets). Mon: 🍿🍿🍿 | Tue: 🍿🍿🍿🍿🍿 | Wed: 🍿🍿🍿🍿. How many packets were sold in all?
Bal Mela balloons sold (key 🎈 = 5). Mon: 🎈🎈🎈🎈 | Tue: 🎈🎈🎈 | Wed: 🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈. How many balloons were sold on Wednesday?
Bal Mela balloons sold (key 🎈 = 5). Mon: 🎈🎈🎈🎈 | Tue: 🎈🎈🎈 | Wed: 🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈. How many balloons were sold in all?
Popcorn (🍿 = 10): Mon 3, Tue 5, Wed 4. Balloons (🎈 = 5): Mon 4, Tue 3, Wed 6. What were Monday's total sales of both items?
Using the same charts, which day had the biggest total sales of both items?
quiz.explain: Mon 30 + 20 = 50. Tue 50 + 15 = 65. Wed 40 + 30 = 70. Wednesday is highest.

quiz.q: Why should you check the key before reading a pictograph?
options: Each symbol may stand for more than 1

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know the busiest day at the Bal Mela. How should Gappu use the pictographs?
teach.praise: Use the key, add both items for each day, and the biggest total is the busiest day!
teach.nudge: How do you find each day's total, and then the busiest day?

topics.title: Bal Mela: comparing items and completing tables

learn.hook: On Wednesday, 40 popcorn packets and 30 balloons were sold. Which sold more, and by how much?
points: To compare two items on the same day, subtract the smaller number from the bigger one.
To complete a table from a pictograph, read each row with the key and write the number.
Check the table: the totals in the table must match the pictograph.
A completed table makes it easy to answer questions quickly.

example.q: On Tuesday, popcorn 50 packets and balloons 15. How many more popcorn packets?

learn.reallife: After a mela, teachers make a table of all sales to report to the principal.

games.title: Fill the table: popcorn 🍿 = 10 (Mon 3, Tue 5, Wed 4 symbols), balloons 🎈 = 5 (Mon 4, Tue 3 symbols)
Comparing on the same day
items: On Monday, popcorn (30) sold 10 more than balloons (20).
On Tuesday, balloons sold more than popcorn.
On Wednesday, popcorn sold 10 more than balloons.
To compare two items, we add them.
We subtract to find how many more.
A table must match the pictograph.

quiz.q: On Tuesday, popcorn sold 50 packets and balloons 15. How many more popcorn packets than balloons?
On Monday, popcorn 30 and balloons 20. How many more popcorn?
Bal Mela balloons sold (key 🎈 = 5). Mon: 🎈🎈🎈🎈 | Tue: 🎈🎈🎈 | Wed: 🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈🎈. Fill the table: balloons sold on Monday = ?
Bal Mela popcorn sales (key 🍿 = 10 packets). Mon: 🍿🍿🍿 | Tue: 🍿🍿🍿🍿🍿 | Wed: 🍿🍿🍿🍿. Fill the table: popcorn sold on Wednesday = ?
A table says bangles: Mon 25, Tue 40, Wed 35. Key 💍 = 5. How many symbols for Tuesday?
Bangles: Mon 25, Tue 40, Wed 35. Key 💍 = 5. How many symbols for Monday?
On Wednesday, balloons 30, bangles 35. How many more bangles?
A table shows popcorn total 120 but the pictograph shows 3 + 5 + 4 symbols with 🍿 = 10. Is the table right?

teach.ask: Gappu has to fill a table from the Bal Mela pictograph and compare items. Explain how.
teach.praise: Multiply symbols by the key to fill the table, then subtract to compare. Done!
teach.nudge: How do you turn symbols into numbers, and how do you compare two items?
